model_annotations.Bulgarian: This plot illustrates the absolute mean of hidden states across layers for three different conditions, titled "Hidden State Mean." The x-axis represents "Layer" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents "Abs Mean" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to approximately 4.5, with tick marks at intervals of 1.0. The first line, shown in blue with a dashed line style, represents "hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71." It starts near 0.05 at layer 0, rises slightly to around 0.2–0.3 in the range of layers 2–7, remains relatively steady around 0.2–0.3 through layer 10, then begins increasing more steeply from approximately 0.4 at layer 12 to around 0.5 at layer 15, reaching approximately 0.9 at layer 18, then sharply escalating to roughly 2.2 at layer 20 and approximately 2.6 at layer 23, with a notable spike above 4.0 near layer 21. The second line, shown in orange with a dotted line style, represents "hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05." It remains very close to 0 throughout all layers, with only a very slight increase toward the final layers, reaching approximately 0.05–0.1 by layer 23. The third line, shown in green with a solid line style, represents "hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04." It similarly stays very close to 0 across all layers, with a marginal increase to approximately 0.05–0.1 near layer 23, closely tracking the orange dotted line throughout.
